note_fixes: Amos 3:8: the verse has a dash, not a gap; quote it as "The Lord GOD has spoken-who will not prophesy?" with no ellipsis
concepts.why: all readers: otherwise sound; the note must be an exact quotation, and an ellipsis where the verse has a dash is not one

concepts.name: I am sending you
concepts.why: secular scholar / Baptist / Reformed: only Isaiah 6:8 says 'Here am I. Send me!'; the others are God's sending (Exod 3:10, Jer 1:7, Ezek 2:3) or a call (1 Sam 3:10, Amos 7:15), so the name says more than its passages; 'I am sending you' (Exod 3:10, Ezek 2:3, cf. Jer 1:7) is the common words. Galatians 1:15 is cut off mid-clause before any sending, and set beside Jeremiah 1:5 it makes Paul a prophet in the site's voice, which Reformed/cessationist and Catholic/Orthodox readers would take as a side; Paul's call belongs with the apostles' texts, not here

secular scholar: the name is 'Return to Me' and Isaiah 1:16-17 says to wash, stop evil, seek justice, with no word of returning; it shares the subject, not the words, and it is the same call as 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' (Isa 1:11 is already there). Keep Isa 55:7 and Ezek 18:32 which name return/repent

Jewish reader / secular scholar / Reformed: 'Who has believed our message?' says no one believed, not that they hear and do not understand, so it shares only the topic of rejection with this name; it is also the verse of the most contested chapter of the Hebrew Bible, and John 12:38 already quotes it in concept 22 in its own words. Dropping it keeps the Isaiah 53 question out of this concept

concepts.name: They persecuted the prophets
concepts.why: all readers: 'Who kills the prophets' (Matt 23:37) is said of killing, but 2 Chronicles 36:16 says mocked and scoffed and Matthew 5:12 says persecuted, so the name says more than two passages. 'They persecuted the prophets before you' is Matthew 5:12's own words and covers killing (Neh 9:26, 1 Kgs 19:10, Jer 26:23), mocking and persecuting alike. Jewish reader: 'Who' as a heading can also read as a collective charge; the OT texts here (Neh 9:26, 2 Chr 36:16) show it is Israel's own narrators saying it, so the passages stay

concepts.name: The prophets of old
concepts.why: Jewish reader / secular scholar: 'The former prophets' is the standing name for Joshua through Kings in the Hebrew canon, so as a heading it suggests that division; 'The prophets of old' (Jer 28:8) is the texts' own words with no canon claim. Acts 15:15 is cut off before the citation, is not a prophet citing an earlier prophet, and James's use of Amos 9:11 is where Reformed, dispensational, Catholic and Orthodox readers part on Israel and the church; set among prophets citing prophets it reads as one side. Amos 9:11 stays in concept 20 as the text's own words

Jewish reader / secular scholar / Baptist (dispensational): Micah 5:2 names no throne and no David, so under 'The throne of David' it is placed by the Matthew 2 reading, which is exactly the OT-points-to-NT identification the site must not make in its own voice; the verse is not cut by anything the concept needs. Isaiah 11:1 names Jesse, not David, and is borderline; keep it only because Jesse is David's father in 1 Samuel and 'Branch' recurs in Jer 23:5. Consider adding Psalm 132:11 or Jeremiah 33:17, which name David's throne in so many words. Luke 1:32 and Acts 2:30 stay, as each is the text's own claim to the throne

concepts.name: Prepare the way
concepts.why: Jewish reader / secular scholar / Baptist: 'A voice of one calling in the wilderness' is Isaiah 40:3, whose own setting is the return from exile, but the site is using the form in which Matthew 3:3 and John 1:23 apply it; heading Isaiah 40:3, Malachi 3:1 and 4:5 with that phrase tells the reader in the site's voice that these OT lines are the voice John was. 'Prepare the way' is in Isa 40:3, Mal 3:1, Mark 1:2, Matt 3:3 and Luke 1:17 alike, is neutral, and the NT identifications stay in the notes as the NT's own words (Matt 3:3, Mark 1:2, Matt 11:14, Luke 1:17, John 1:23). Order unchanged

Jewish reader / secular scholar / Baptist (dispensational) / Reformed: the name is Jeremiah's 'I will make a new covenant', and Luke 22:20 shares the words 'new covenant' but does not say it is Jeremiah's or who it is made with; grouping it here makes the site assert that Jesus's cup is Jeremiah 31's covenant, which is the exact point where Israel-and-church readings divide. Hebrews 8:8 stays because it quotes Jeremiah 31:31 in its own words. Luke 22:20 is held by the Covenant theme in its own wording. Ezekiel 36:26 names a new heart and spirit but not a covenant; consider Ezekiel 37:26 ('an everlasting covenant') beside it

note_fixes: Revelation 21:5: the note joins two sentences with an ellipsis; use "Behold, I make all things new." (or the two in full) as the verse gives them
concepts.why: all readers: the concept meets the last-concept rule (the theme's own words of hope, with the dark concepts - the case, the plumb line, killed and mocked prophets, hearing without understanding - left intact earlier). Only the note is not an exact quotation

secondary_or_links: Links: add the Sacrifice theme (whatever its title on the site) - concept 11 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' is held there too, and the drafter's own account says so; without the link a reader of that concept has no door to it
Secondary 'The Law -> the Prophets' is fine (Matt 7:12, 11:13, Luke 16:16, 24:44 are all NT's own words); Luke 24:44 repeats concept 23, which is harmless
Secondary 'The prophet -> the nations': Jonah 1:2 names neither prophet nor nations; keep only if the card is shown as Jonah being sent, otherwise swap for Jeremiah 25:15-17 or Amos 1:3

Order: concepts 20-23 run OT promise lines into NT claim lines, which reads as a sequence from promise to fulfilment; the owner's ruling on overlap and ordering stands, but if the order is ever reshuffled, 22 and 23 (NT only) should stay together so each is plainly the NT's own testimony

missing.why: the messenger formula is the most frequent sign of a prophetic speech in the texts and is not named by any concept (concept 2 is the formula of the word coming, not of the word delivered)

missing.sub_theme: Eat this scroll / I ate them
missing.why: the word received and written down: the scroll Ezekiel eats, Jeremiah's 'Your words were found, and I ate them', and the command to write; concept 5 holds only Habakkuk 2:2 and Daniel 7:1 for writing

missing.sub_theme: Stand in the breach / Do not pray for this people
missing.why: the prophet as one who prays for the people (Abraham is called a prophet in Gen 20:7); the texts develop it as part of the prophetic office and it is the other half of the watchman and the case

missing.sub_theme: A famine of hearing the words of the LORD
missing.why: the dark counterpart the texts themselves name: no vision, no prophet, no answer. Without it the theme shows the word always present; the site's rule is that nothing dark is left out. It also sits beside 'I desire mercy' and 'Be ever hearing' as a consequence the texts record
